verdictLine: QUALIFIED WITH LIMITS: instrumented whole-terminal CPU baseline; unequal DOM cell width/default scrollbar; endpoint-only process coverage and logical settlement, with no presentation or whole-device energy proof
reviewType: Independent review of saved benchmark evidence, not a code review
qualifiedScope: The measured all-Chrome instructions and kernel CPU-energy ratios of the instrumented, same-configured-grid, full-retained-text whole-terminal pipelines on this Mac session. The numerical claim reproduces and passes the prospectively registered baseline acceptance rule with the limits below.
notQualifiedClaims: Identical visible DOM element sizes or equal-size raster work
Isolated DOM-renderer efficiency after normalizing library-default auxiliary layers
Complete detection of processes born and exited wholly between snapshots
No post-endpoint layout/device work or physical presentation completion
GPU-device, display or whole-device power savings
An overhead-corrected uninstrumented ratio, a candidate KEEP or a cross-workload/cross-host claim

acceptanceReview.sameActorScreenshotHashesGate: Not a registered cross-library counterpart-baseline gate. Xterm PNG variation is two scrollbar-edge pixels; logical oracle passes.

findings.title: All claimed native ratios and all four paired directions reproduce from cumulative per-PID readings
findings.detail: Integer subtraction was repeated independently for every PID, then summed by CDP process type before forming adjacent chronological pairs. The evaluation stores indexes in numerator/denominator order for reversed pairs (3,2 and 7,6); these are the same registered adjacent pairs, not different window selection. The quoted CPU ratio is native rusage CPU time. The separately recomputed CDP ratio is slightly different.

findings.title: Registration predates acquisition; eight windows are retained exactly once
findings.detail: registeredAt, Linux mtime and ctime precede driver start. Local protocol bytes hash to the hash in the Mac stage receipt and raw index; the raw embedded protocol matches. The registered DOM/XDOM/XDOM/DOM order repeated twice is exactly the eight complete raw rows. There are no missing, failed, replaced or extra R05 windows. The preserved output archive has the same raw index and exactly eight screenshots. Earlier stock acquisitions fail dependency import before browser measurement; shared R01 fails its seal check before launch; shared R02 was abandoned with zero windows. Only one R05 rolling acquisition appears in the Mac turn ledger.

findings.title: Equal public work and the entire retained-text oracle can be reconstructed independently
findings.detail: The frozen logs and registered rolling chunk algorithm reconstruct all 900 input chunks, wrapping at 40 columns. The only non-ASCII fixture character is the single-column en dash. Independent reconstruction produces the exact saved full-history digest, history head/tail, normalized visible text and row counts in all 136 target readbacks. Trailing whitespace normalization is explicitly registered and necessary because native visibleLines pads rows. Public bytes include the 19-byte reset. Both requested DOM implementations were mounted: native rendererFactory selects DomTerminalRenderer and raw runtime diagnostics say dom; xterm selects the stock DOM renderer, loads no WebGL addon, and records no canvas elements. Font loading is awaited before actor construction.

findings.title: Configured grids and fonts match, but actual DOM cell width and the scrollbar layer do not
findings.detail: All 17 host sections are 380 by 260 CSS pixels, share scale 0.5803303303303303, and lie inside the viewport. Native uses a deliberately transparent 560 by 456 device-pixel canvas as its DOM geometry anchor; it is not a renderer fallback. The saved native DOM code sizes the visible grid from the same fitted cell dimensions, implying 280 by 228 CSS pixels and 7-pixel cells. Xterm records a 288 by 228 CSS grid with 7.2-pixel cells. Native compresses glyph spacing using cell-width minus 1ch, whereas xterm retains fractional cell width. Native's visible grid is 2.7778% narrower. The visible DOM div itself was not included in the geometry snapshot, so its bounds are source-inferred and screenshot-supported rather than directly recorded. Both screenshots have the same text and wrapping, but do not prove equal-size raster work. The gray right-edge boxes in the xterm screenshots are scrollbar thumbs, not evidence of a different cursor: they lie at the host right edge outside the text grid; xterm's saved viewport constructs a default vertical scrollbar, while native reports scrollbarVisible=false. These library-default auxiliary layers are part of the measured whole-terminal result. A strict equal-visible-size or renderer-only claim is not qualified by this dataset.

findings.title: All endpoint coverage checks pass; process events wholly between boundaries remain unobservable
findings.detail: Each window has exactly seven Chrome PIDs: three renderer processes, one GPU, one browser, one network service and one storage service. PID/type/start sets agree, all reader requests cover all PIDs, exit stamps are zero at both endpoints, and all cumulative deltas are nonnegative. Every acquisition has ordered node CDP request/completion and native per-PID brackets. The reader is the one owned PID outside all measured Chrome sets; Node, Playwright and the in-process fixture server also run outside Chrome. No partial aggregate is used. There is no continuous process-birth/exit log; therefore the stronger statement that absolutely no process was born and exited inside a window is not proven. Start identities and brackets do not close that endpoint-only blind spot. All 29 owned PIDs are recorded dead after browser/reader/fixture shutdown and the controller's final process search is empty.

findings.title: Power/load/display and scheduled-turn guards pass; unregistered background work is not independently inventoried
findings.detail: Outer admission records AC and load 2.44 below the outer threshold 3. All per-actor AC/load admissions pass the saved driver threshold 4, including 3.09 and 3.13, and every post-actor power check is on AC. Each pre-window idle display probe records visible/focused state and 120 valid positive periods with median 16.6 or 16.7 ms. The pinned headed Chrome version is 154.0.8037.93 and backend data names Apple M1 / ANGLE Metal, with no SwiftShader. The Mac turn log has no overlapping scheduled research turn during this acquisition. This does not prove absence of every owner/background process: no OS-wide process inventory or continuous power/display sampling is saved. The guard only demonstrates the registered sampled conditions and coordinated turn exclusion.

findings.title: Logical settlement and visible-row work pass; GPU/device presentation and post-endpoint layout debt are not measured
findings.detail: Native completes 901 core writes, frame publications, updates, ACKs and renderer callbacks per target, with 10,812 painted rows / 432,480 cells, zero dirty state, equal accepted/current revisions, no rebuild and no pending frame/timer/link resolution. Xterm completes 901 parser calls and write callbacks, 1,802 DOM renderRows callbacks, and has empty write buffer, zero pending bytes and no recorded render animation-frame handle. Both libraries paint viewport rows rather than the 111,328 retained history rows; saved xterm and native DOM loops are bounded by the same 12-row grid, and all panels are on screen. Both have cursor blink disabled, receive the same cursor-hide bytes before warmup, and have accessibility disabled. The fixture has no URLs or OSC-link sequences and native pending-link state is clear; no active link-hover work is established. The endpoint includes a common two-RAF logical drain and snapshots, not a compositor/device fence. There is no immediate post-endpoint trace or residual-work bracket proving zero delayed layout/paint/device work; screenshots and full-text readback occur later, outside counters. Observed native stock durations are 15.0497-15.0502 seconds versus xterm 15.0648-15.1167 seconds for equal 900 paid ticks, so ghostty did not end early by skipping ticks. Renderer callback counts are real implementation differences, not equal-work counters.

findings.title: The qualified observation is one instrumented whole-pipeline CPU-energy baseline, not a product optimization or device-power verdict
findings.detail: The validated reader reports retired work and the kernel recount CPU-energy estimate, including CPU execution in the GPU process but excluding physical GPU-device, display and non-Chrome energy. The researcher explicitly registered these bounds and did not claim a candidate KEEP. Runtime observer overhead remains uncalibrated and differs in the number of wrapped internal calls between libraries; raw directions are valid for this instrumented harness, not an overhead-corrected uninstrumented estimate. Results cover one Mac session and this rolling full-stream condition only. Native renderer effective clocks and P-core shares differ from xterm, which confirms why CPU seconds alone are not the efficiency gate. No fresh browser replay, reader ABI qualification, other-host test, source change, merge or deployment was performed by this reviewer.
